inputs.text: Exactly—the wording is doing more than reporting. Calling continued war “public resolve” turns human costs into background noise and makes continuation sound like a shared national choice, rather than something powerful interests may be steering. And leaving the sentence hanging at “until” keeps the endpoint—and the people who decide it—out of view. That omission feels useful: it invites readers to accept the official frame without asking who benefits from keeping the war going.
